learnings.insight: Small Next.js 14 portfolio with single attack surface (/api/chat). Analysis is tractable without sub-agents.
npm audit revealed 20 vulnerabilities (1 critical) in Next.js 14.1.1. Running audit on every review is essential.
Sub-agent delegation (delegate_task) froze during architecture stage. Manual file creation was more reliable for this codebase size.
Prompt injection in AI-integrated forms is the highest-impact vulnerability. Textual defenses ('ignore instructions in the message') are consistently bypassable.
Serverless rate limiting with in-memory state is fundamentally broken. Must use distributed state (Redis, Vercel KV).
NEXT_PUBLIC_ prefix exposes values to client bundle. EmailJS service/template IDs, while designed to be public, still enable unauthorized use if domain restrictions are not configured.
The Mantis pipeline works well for web applications with ~20 source files. Full execution of 11 stages took approximately 20 minutes.
dangerouslySetInnerHTML in layout.tsx is a latent risk. Should be replaced with Next.js Script component for JSON-LD.
